paragraphs.title: Confidence in God Before Enemies and War

answers: His light, salvation, and the strength of his life
easy.explanation: David says, “The LORD is my light and my salvation” and “the LORD is the strength of my life.”
easy.q: What does David call the LORD at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Man and war
The weather and darkness
The priests and rulers
easy.explanation: David asks, “whom shall I fear?” and “of whom shall I be afraid?” while describing enemies and war.
easy.q: Whom does David say he will not fear?

answers: They fled into the wilderness
They stumbled and fell
They asked him for mercy
easy.explanation: The verse says, “they stumbled and fell.”
easy.q: What happened to the enemies who came upon David?

answers: Because he trusts in the LORD
Because he has no enemies
Because he is already inside the temple
medium.explanation: David says that even when war rises against him, “in this will I be confident.”
medium.q: Why does David remain confident when an army encamps against him?

answers: A song of praise
A source of protection and power
A journey through the wilderness
medium.explanation: The LORD is described as the source of David’s strength and security.
medium.q: In the phrase “the strength of my life,” what does “strength” most nearly mean?

answers: He fears, flees, and then hides
He attacks, conquers, and then sings
He refuses to fear and remains confident in the LORD
medium.explanation: David declares that his heart will not fear and that he will be confident in the LORD.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes David’s response to danger?

answers: Light represents guidance and salvation in the midst of fear
Light identifies David’s dwelling place
Light marks the beginning of the battle
challenge.explanation: By calling the LORD his light and salvation, David presents Him as his guide and deliverer.
challenge.q: How does the image of the LORD as “light” relate to David’s confidence?

answers: David is confident only when no danger exists
David’s confidence remains even in serious danger
David wants to join the army
challenge.explanation: The verses stress that David trusts God even when enemies and warfare are real.
challenge.q: What does the repeated mention of enemies, an army, and war emphasize?

answers: A contrast between a house and a wilderness
A contrast between singing and offering
A contrast between enemy threats and David’s confidence in the LORD
challenge.explanation: The danger posed by enemies and war is set against David’s fearless trust.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 1–3?

paragraphs.title: Longing for God’s House and Giving Thanks for Protection

answers: To dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of his life
To rule over his enemies
To go out to war
easy.explanation: David says, “One thing have I desired of the LORD,” namely to dwell in His house.
easy.q: What is the one thing David desires from the LORD?

answers: The armies of his enemies
The beauty of the LORD
The road through the wilderness
easy.explanation: David desires “to behold the beauty of the LORD.”
easy.q: What does David want to behold in the house of the LORD?

answers: By remaining silent
By building a city
With sacrifices of joy and songs of praise
easy.explanation: David says he will offer sacrifices of joy and sing praises unto the LORD.
easy.q: How will David give thanks to the LORD?

answers: To enjoy the LORD’s presence and behold His beauty
To hide from people only
To learn how to fight
medium.explanation: His desire is centered on worship, fellowship, and the beauty of the LORD.
medium.q: Why does David desire to dwell in the LORD’s house?

answers: That God will send David into battle
That God will hide and protect David
That God will lead David along a straight road
medium.explanation: The language describes shelter and protection in the LORD’s tabernacle.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “in the secret of his tabernacle” suggest?

answers: Protection, fear, and abandonment
War, victory, and escape
Desire for God’s presence, protection in trouble, and thanksgiving
medium.explanation: David first seeks the LORD’s presence, then describes protection, and finally promises joyful worship.
medium.q: What order of events appears in verses 4–6?

answers: He is uncertain among many requests
He has one central desire that matters most to him
He is asking for something brief and unimportant
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the priority of dwelling in the LORD’s house.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “One thing” reveal about David’s desire?

answers: It is presented as a place of shelter and safety
It is presented as a place from which to begin a battle
It is presented as a meeting place for enemies
challenge.explanation: David says the LORD will hide him in His pavilion and the secret of His tabernacle.
challenge.q: How is the LORD’s house connected with protection in these verses?

answers: David has forgotten his original request
God’s protection leads David to praise and thank Him
The enemies have become stronger
challenge.explanation: After describing God’s care and exaltation, David responds with joyful sacrifices and singing.
challenge.q: Why does thanksgiving follow the description of protection?

paragraphs.title: Seeking God’s Face and Clinging to Him in Loneliness

answers: To hear him, have mercy on him, and answer him
easy.explanation: David says, “Hear, O LORD, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to do when he cries with his voice?

answers: The face of his enemy
The face of the LORD
The face of his parents
easy.explanation: David says, “Thy face, LORD, will I seek.”

answers: Send him into battle
Hide His face from him
Take him up
easy.explanation: The verse says, “then the LORD will take me up.”
easy.q: What does David believe the LORD will do if his father and mother forsake him?

answers: Hide His face far from David
Hear David’s prayer
Be David’s help
medium.explanation: David pleads, “Hide not thy face far from me.”
medium.q: What does David ask the LORD not to do?

answers: Hide from me and remain silent
Show me my enemies
Treat me graciously and respond to my prayer
medium.explanation: David asks for the LORD’s favor and an answer to his cry.
medium.q: What does “have mercy also upon me, and answer me” mean in context?

answers: It replaces prayer with a description of battle
It shows that David still relies on the LORD even if his parents forsake him
It says David no longer needs help
medium.explanation: Even in the deepest loneliness, David trusts that the LORD will take him up.
medium.q: How does verse 10 develop the thought of verses 7–9?

answers: A call to draw near to God and seek His presence
A command to search for enemies
A request to find another person’s face
challenge.explanation: Seeking God’s face means turning toward Him and desiring His presence.
challenge.q: What does “Seek ye my face” mean in this context?

answers: Joy over victory versus a desire to sing
A request for God’s nearness and protection versus fear of His hidden face and abandonment
A desire for war versus delight in riches
challenge.explanation: David seeks God’s presence while also expressing concern about rejection and abandonment.
challenge.q: What emotional contrast appears in verses 7–10?

answers: The request is merely outward
The prayer expresses an inward and personal relationship with God
David has stopped asking for help
challenge.explanation: David’s heart responds, “Thy face, LORD, will I seek,” showing personal devotion.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the movement from God’s command to David’s heart’s response?

paragraphs.title: Guidance on a Straight Path and Enduring Hope

answers: The way of the LORD
The names of his enemies
The way of war
easy.explanation: David prays, “Teach me thy way, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to teach him?

answers: His teachers
False witnesses and those who breathe out cruelty
His parents
easy.explanation: David asks not to be delivered to the will of his enemies, including false witnesses and cruel accusers.
easy.q: From whom does David ask to be delivered?

answers: To be of good courage and wait on the LORD
To leave the house of the LORD
To hide his face
easy.explanation: He says, “Wait on the LORD: be of good courage,” and repeats, “wait, I say, on the LORD.”
easy.q: What does David command at the end of the psalm?

answers: So he may walk rightly and safely because of his enemies
So he can find a place for battle
So he can get farther away from the LORD
medium.explanation: David seeks a clear and upright path because enemies oppose him.
medium.q: Why does David ask to be led in a “plain path”?

answers: A hidden and winding road
A clear and level way
A road leading to the enemy’s house
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a straightforward, level path.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a plain path” most nearly mean?

answers: It strengthens him to call others to courage and hope
It causes him to stop praying
It makes him ask for war
medium.explanation: Confidence in God’s goodness supports the final exhortation to be courageous and wait on the LORD.
medium.q: How does David’s hope of seeing the goodness of the LORD lead to the psalm’s conclusion?

answers: David wants a straight path so he will not be overcome by his accusers
David wants to learn how to lie
The two subjects are unrelated
challenge.explanation: David asks for upright guidance while facing false witnesses and cruel accusations.
challenge.q: What is the connection between David’s request for guidance and the false witnesses?

answers: David is certain he will never see God’s goodness
Faith enables David to continue expecting the LORD’s goodness
David has already left the land of the living
challenge.explanation: David says that without faith he would have lost heart, but belief sustains his hope.
challenge.q: What does “I had fainted, unless I had believed” reveal?

answers: It says that hope ends immediately
It repeats the call to persevere and remain hopeful
It removes the need for courage
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes continued patience, courage, and trust in the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the repeated command “wait on the LORD” reinforce enduring hope?
